reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a zero-coding flash-loan arbitrage bot as capable of making substantial money and instructs viewers to deploy a contract and send BNB to its address. It further tells viewers to confirm MetaMask transactions and retry with additional BNB if the first amount does not work, creating a concrete money-transfer and participation flow. the available video evidence does not establish ownership, actual returns, fund recovery, or transaction outcome.

citations.quote: Flash loan crypto arbitrage bots have been making a lot of money!
Today we bring you a zero coding needed flash loan arbitrage bot!
Click on Deploy & Run transactions and set "ENVIRONMENT" to Injected Web3.
17. Send BNB to the deployed contract
19. Now, Click "action" (red box) to execute the Flash Loan.

opening.argument: Judge, the description does not present flash loans as effortless or risk-free. It explains that they must be repaid within one transaction and explicitly warns that exploits have been used to steal millions. The funding instruction is tied to initiating a swap, while the later note says fees may vary and the first amount may not work. That context supports reading this as a technically risky procedure being described, not an unconditional promise of returns.

citations.quote: flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and steal millions of dollars.
A flash loan has to be borrowed and repaid within the same blockchain transaction.
17. Send BNB to the deployed contract
because fees may be different from day to day.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that viewers are told to fund a contract, but that instruction alone does not establish who controls the contract or where its funds ultimately go. Its cited instruction to click an action describes the purported execution step, not a verified return or an explicit guarantee. The description also acknowledges that the procedure may fail at the first funding amount.

citations.quote: 17. Send BNB to the deployed contract
19. Now, Click "action" (red box) to execute the Flash Loan.
if it doesn't work with 0.2 BNB try to send another 0.2 BNB

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning concerns exploits against DeFi protocols, not the viewer's risk from funding this particular contract. A caveat about fees does not offset the instruction to send BNB and then send more if it does not work. The description couples those payments to a bot promoted as a money-making opportunity; no verified return is needed to recognize that solicitation.

citations.quote: Flash loan crypto arbitrage bots have been making a lot of money!

Note: if it doesn't work with 0.2 BNB try to send another 0.2 BNB

opening.argument: Judge, most of the presentation walks through an operational demonstration: create a Solidity file, select a compiler version, compile it, deploy it and use the resulting contract. The speaker also corrects himself about where the contract was launched. Those details make the screen activity intelligible as a tutorial rather than merely an appeal for money. The footage and narration show a workflow, but neither establishes that the displayed result is reproducible for viewers.

citations.quote: 3. Click on File Explorers and click "Create New File ".
8. Click on the Solidity Compiler and then click the blue button "Compile flashloans.sol"
Oh no, not Pancake swap. We launched it on the B&B Smart Chain.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution cites real participation steps, but steps to deploy and invoke a contract are also what an operational demonstration would contain. Its opening does not establish that the demonstrated contract was controlled by someone other than its deployer, or that the claimed result actually occurred. The narrator explicitly frames the later action as running the contract just made.

citations.quote: Click on Deploy & Run transactions and set "ENVIRONMENT" to Injected Web3.
This is to run the smart loan contract we've just made.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial format is precisely how the promotion directs participation: the viewer is told to paste code from a linked source, deploy it, send BNB to the contract and execute its action. A walkthrough does not make those funding instructions incidental, particularly when the speaker presents the result as money made. The visible workflow does not verify the contract's safety or actual returns.

19. Now, Click "action" (red box) to execute the Flash Loan.
look at that amount we just made.

opening.argument: Judge, the requested payment is described as funding a newly deployed contract to run a swap, not as buying a membership or paying the presenter. The speaker calls it gas money sent to the contract address and describes the borrowing as conditional on the program finding a profit. The record does not establish the recipient's ownership, a guaranteed yield, or that the displayed wallet activity proves any return. On what is actually shown, this can be read as promotion of a software workflow with transaction costs, not proof of a deceptive payment scheme.

citations.quote: 16. Copy the address of the newly deployed contract. 17. Send BNB to the deployed contract
to initiate the swap 0.2+ (0.3 up is better as you will get a bigger amount in each swap
And you're going to have to send gas money over to the contract address to run it.
if this program finds a profit on Pancake Swap against SWAP.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's strongest point is the repeat-payment instruction. Still, that note attributes the retry to variable fees; it does not identify an external payee or document what the contract does with the BNB. The claim that bots have made money is broad, not a stated guarantee that this viewer's transaction will profit. Those limits matter when inferring a deceptive mechanism from the instructions alone.

citations.quote: because fees may be different from day to day.
Flash loan crypto arbitrage bots have been making a lot of money!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing ownership and outcome evidence does not erase the observable funding mechanism. Viewers are directed to obtain code from the supplied link, deploy it, send BNB to the resulting contract and add more BNB if the first amount fails. The description even encourages a larger transfer for a bigger amount in each swap. Calling the transfer gas money does not establish that the contract is safe or that viewers will recover their funds.
